name: Lavender Pink
lede: Lavender Pink is a bright, warm purple-pink that sits between its two namesakes, closer to orchid than to either lavender or pink alone.

sections.title: Between two flowers
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd color survey is the only source we hold for this exact hex, and its log does not record who first paired the two flower and family words or why [1]. The combination follows a common pattern in crowd-sourced names: two familiar color words joined to describe a shade that sits between [[lavender|Lavender]] and [[pink|Pink]] [1].

In practice the swatch leans warmer and more saturated than most lavenders, closer to [[orchid|Orchid]] than to the pale purple the word "lavender" usually brings to mind [2]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file it as a brilliant purple [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact purple-pink covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. A color this bright and this saturated sits outside the range aged oil paint and varnish typically produce [3]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [3].
